title: Jobber Pricing 2026: Plans, Add-Ons and Total Cost
summary: Jobber pricing includes three tiers starting at $49 monthly, though full costs exceed the base rate.
body_markdown:
## Connect Jobber to Other Tools with Activepieces


When Jobber's information needs to reach other apps, Activepieces passes it along for you: it connects to 747 integrations, and its MIT-licensed core is free to self-host.


It's worth building only when the copying it replaces costs you more than the afternoon it takes to set up. Doing nothing has a price too: someone retyping paid invoices into a spreadsheet every Friday.


### What Jobber already connects to natively


Check Jobber's own app marketplace first, because a built-in connection costs you no setup and nothing extra to maintain.


Jobber lists accounting links such as QuickBooks Online and Xero, calendar syncing, email marketing through Mailchimp, and a connection to Zapier, another automation service. Confirm the current list inside your account, since vendors change it.


If the thing you want is on that list, use it and stop reading here.


Activepieces earns its place only for the gaps: a chat alert, a custom spreadsheet, or a tool Jobber's never heard of, and its free plan's 1,000 credits a month are enough to try each of them at no cost.


Then look in Activepieces' list of connectors, which it calls pieces and of which roughly 60% are community-contributed, and search for Jobber. I can't point you to a confirmed Jobber integration, so don't plan around one. If it's missing, you have a fallback.


Without a ready-made connector, Jobber can still send a webhook, a short message fired the moment something happens.


Activepieces bills one credit per flow run however many steps follow, so the ten-step version costs what the two-step shortcut does, unlike Zapier's per-task or Make's per-module billing.


Activepieces can catch that message with a webhook trigger, or reach into Jobber with an HTTP request step.


It takes a little more patience than a ready-made connector, but it works, and since every plan, free included, allows unlimited flows, a second flow adds no plan fee.


### Example Jobber invoice to spreadsheet workflow


Take from it that the flow's one trigger and two actions, small enough for one person to build and check.


1. Create a flow in Activepieces and choose a webhook trigger. Copy the address it gives you.
2. In Jobber's developer settings, register that address to receive an invoice-paid event.
3. Add a spreadsheet step that writes a new row: client name, invoice number, amount, date.
4. Add a chat step that posts a one-line note to your office channel.
5. Pay a test invoice and confirm the row and message both appear.


That's the work. Afterward, watch the flow for a few weeks, because a broken connection fails quietly.


Skip all of this if you close a handful of invoices a week. Typing them by hand is cheaper than owning another system, and your accounting link may already do the job.
